subject: Clarification: cloud provider SOC mapping + bridge letter request
messages:
From: Maya R. (Infranet Security) <maya.r@infranet.com>

Cc: laura.parker@parker-audit.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SOC 2 mapping to AWS + bridge letter for carve-out

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call yesterday. Two follow-ups from our compliance team and external auditor:

1) Can you confirm which AWS SOC 2 report(s) Redwood relied on during the audit window (Jan 1 2026 – Dec 31 2026), specifically for the following services: EC2, EBS, S3, EKS, and IAM? Our auditor needs the exact report IDs and timeframes to validate subservice coverage.

2) For scoped carve-outs: we saw a note in the SOC 2 that certain managed cloud components were carved out (network transit and host-level patching performed by AWS). Can Redwood provide a short bridge letter that: (a) lists the carved-out responsibilities, (b) maps shared responsibilities between Redwood and AWS, and (c) confirms where Redwood has compensating controls?

Deliverables: preferred is a PDF SOC 2 mapping table and a 1–2 page bridge letter draft. Could you also attach a list of subprocessors used during the audit window?

We are aiming to close the gap on our vendor assessment by May 6. Laura (cc) will incorporate into the Infranet report.

Thanks — appreciate the help.

Best,
Maya
Information Security Manager
Infranet Inc

Hi all — attaching the draft items per Dylan's plan. Summary below.

Attachments (attached to this thread):
- Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026_redacted.pdf (PDF)
- redwood_aws_mapping_table_2026.csv (CSV) — maps Redwood control IDs to AWS SOC report IDs and control descriptions
- draft_bridge_letter_infranet.docx (DOCX) — 2-page draft for your review
- subprocessors_2026-export.csv (CSV) — names, purposes, and engagement start dates

Key clarifications (short):
- AWS coverage: During the audit window we relied primarily on AWS SOC 2 reports for the following services and report IDs (excerpt):
  * EC2, EBS: AWS SOC 2 report ID: AWS-SOC2-2026-EC2-EBS (covering Jan–Dec 2026)
  * S3: AWS-SOC2-2026-S3 (Jan–Dec 2026)
  * EKS: AWS-SOC2-2026-EKS (Jan–Dec 2026)
  * IAM/Identity services: AWS-SOC2-2026-IDENTITY (Jan–Dec 2026)

- Carve-out summary (as requested):
  * Carved-out by AWS: host OS-level patching, physical datacenter controls, underlying hypervisor maintenance, and certain network transit monitoring.
  * Redwood responsibilities: application-layer logging, model access controls, tenant-level encryption keys (KMS integration), runtime configuration management, and detection/response on our managed endpoints.
  * Compensating controls: where AWS performs a responsibility we maintain redundancy via host-level monitoring agents and an extra layer of configuration management that we own; noted in the mapping table columns.

Next steps:
- Please review the draft bridge letter and mapping table. If Infranet needs a signed/printed bridge letter, we can prepare a finalized PDF and provide a sign-off from Redwood security.
- Laura: happy to take any edits you want to align with the auditor language.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call if it helps move this along.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Head of Security, Redwood Inference

- Mapping table: could you add a column that explicitly states whether the control is "AWS responsibility", "Redwood responsibility", or "Shared" (right now it is implied in notes but we need an explicit flag for our tooling).

- Bridge letter: we will provide suggested wording edits. If possible please include a signature block for an authorized Redwood security officer.

Laura will follow up with any auditor-specific phrasing. We may request a short Zoom on Monday to finalize language.
